response.name:
Bad request — request body validation failed, or the supplied
features span more than one inspection. Validation messages are raw, e.g.:
  - `"data.work_order_name" is required`
  - `"data.work_order_description" is required`
  - `"data.maintenance_flags" must contain at least 1 items`
  - `"data.maintenance_flags" must be an array`
  - `"data.latchel_property_id" is required` (`latchel`)
  - `"data.ok_to_enter" is required` (`rentmanager`)
  - `"data.priority" must be one of [Low, Normal, High]` (`rentmanager`)
  - `"data.work_order_code" is required` (`jenark`)
The cross-inspection guard returns
`Inspection must be consistent. All features should belong to the same inspection.`
The Rent Manager integration also surfaces
`property not synced with integration` and
`No rentmanager integration is configured for this account` as 400
when its preflight checks fail.

Internal server error. Sources:
  - Unknown `provider` — `invalid provider` is returned when the path
    parameter is not one of the registered providers. The
    path-parameter `enum` documents the supported set; unsupported
    providers should be rejected before processing.
  - Jenark — `property not synced with Jenark` is returned when the
    property is not synced through the Jenark integration. (The
    analogous Rent Manager check surfaces as 400 — see the 400
    response above.)
  - AppFolio / Rentvine — `Must have work order sync switched ON in
    order to create work orders. Please adjust your data sync
    settings.` is returned when the integration exists but work-order
    sync is disabled.

description.content:
## Mission
At RentCheck, our mission is plain and simple: To make renting fair and transparent for everyone involved. 
RentCheck is a property inspection solution that helps property managers save time and resources with easy self-guided inspections that residents can perform from their smartphone. 

With RentCheck, property managers can avoid tenant coordination, eliminate drive time, and standardize their inspection process. 
We provides real-time visibility to property managers and owners while bringing transparency to the security deposit deduction process.

## API
The RentCheck API lets developers tap into the RentCheck ecosystem, building their own RentCheck-powered applications to enable inspection scheduling and creation and to leverage inspection data for a variety of use cases in the property management, maintenance, and insurance spaces.

The RentCheck REST API supports JSON requests and responses and features a resource-oriented design that generally adheres to the RFC 7321 HTTP/1.1 standard. 
Our API resources provide access to many RentCheck features, including units, buildings, communities, inspections, and residents.

## Credentials
In addition to the Bearer Auth, RentCheck will need to send you an application ID and secret. These are required to generate the required application headers (x-app-id & x-app-secret).
These values can be obtained from the [RentCheck API integration page](https://app.getrentcheck.com/account/integrations/rentcheck-api).

## Rate Limiting
The RentCheck API enforces rate limits to ensure fair usage and prevent abuse. The rate limits are as follows:
- **Requests per second**: 8
- **Requests per minute**: 256
- **Requests per 10 minutes**: 1024

If you exceed the rate limits, you will receive a 429 Too Many Requests response.

## Pagination
When interacting with endpoints that return a list of items, the results are paginated to help manage large data sets efficiently. The following parameters control pagination:
- **page_size** (integer): Defines the number of items returned per page. The maximum allowed value is 250. If a value larger than 250 is provided, it will be automatically clamped to 250. This ensures that the system performs optimally and prevents the server from being overwhelmed by too many items in a single response.
  - **Maximum**: `250`
- **page_number** (integer): Indicates the page number to retrieve. Pagination starts at `page 0`. If not specified, the first page (`page 0`) is returned by default.
### Example Request
```http
GET /api/v1/inspections?page_size=300&page_number=2
```
In this example, although the `page_size` parameter is set to `300` **for a query with 1500 total results**, the system will return only `250` items per page, as `300` exceeds the maximum allowed value.
#### Example Response
```json
{
    "status": 200,
    "data": [...],
    "count": 250,
    "total_results": 1500
}
```
This response shows that the `page_size` has been clamped to `250`, despite the initial request for `300`.
